questions.question: If tourists visit the historic walled city of Harar Jugol, they ______ ancient shrines and unique cultural heritage.
questions.explanation: In Conditional Type 1 sentences describing probable future events, the 'if'-clause takes the Simple Present ('visit') while the result clause takes 'will + base verb' ('will see').

questions.question: Jemal said, 'I enjoy visiting Ethiopian UNESCO heritage sites.' When converted into reported speech, this sentence becomes: 'Jemal said that he ______ visiting Ethiopian UNESCO heritage sites.'
questions.explanation: When reporting direct speech with a past tense reporting verb ('said'), Simple Present verbs ('enjoy') backshift to Simple Past ('enjoyed').

questions.question: Harar Jugol is surrounded by ancient walls constructed to protect the sacred city from invaders. What is the closest contextual meaning of 'fortified'?

options.text: Strengthened or secured with defensive structures

questions.explanation: In Section 7.4 vocabulary, 'fortified' contextually means strengthened, defended, or protected against invasion using walls or barriers.

questions.question: While the students were conducting their science experiment in the school laboratory, all the electric lights suddenly ______.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'go off' means to stop functioning, turn off, or lose electric power suddenly.

questions.question: Complete the dialogue: Abebe: 'In my view, preserving indigenous national heritages promotes tourism and national unity.' Met'elo: '______; our cultural heritage defines our identity.'

options.text: I couldn't agree with you more
I'm afraid I have a different opinion
That makes no sense at all

questions.explanation: 'I couldn't agree with you more' is a standard formal expression used to express strong agreement with an opinion.

questions.question: If I ______ the Minister of Tourism and Culture, I would allocate additional financial resources to restore ancient historical sites across Ethiopia.
questions.explanation: In standard formal English, Second Conditional hypothetical clauses use the subjunctive 'were' for all subjects ('If I were...').

questions.question: Before submitting your final draft of the argumentative essay, you should carefully ______ your written paragraphs to correct grammatical errors.
questions.explanation: The phrasal verb 'go over' means to review, examine, check, or inspect something carefully.

questions.question: Senait said, 'We will visit the Konso Cultural Landscape tomorrow.' In reported speech: Senait said that they would visit the Konso Cultural Landscape ______.
questions.explanation: In reported speech, time expressions referring to the future like 'tomorrow' shift to 'the next day' or 'the following day'.

questions.question: Attaching the prefix 'im-' to the root word 'moral' forms 'immoral'. Which prefix added to 'management' forms a word meaning 'bad or ineffective administration'?
questions.explanation: The prefix 'mis-' signifies bad, wrong, or ill. Combining 'mis-' with 'management' forms 'mismanagement'.

questions.question: Ethiopia will attract millions of international visitors ______ the government and local communities maintain peace and preserve historical monuments.
questions.explanation: 'Provided that' functions as a conditional connector meaning 'on condition that' or 'if'.

questions.question: The Konso Cultural Landscape is celebrated for its stone-walled terraces that protect farmland from soil erosion. What is the contextual meaning of 'vicinities'?
questions.explanation: Contextually in Unit 7, 'vicinities' refers to surrounding areas, neighborhoods, or nearby regions.

questions.question: ______ the regional administration invested in heritage conservation five years ago, the ancient palace walls would not have suffered severe structural collapse.
questions.explanation: In formal inverted Third Conditional sentences, 'If' is omitted and the auxiliary verb 'Had' is inverted with the subject ('Had the regional administration invested...').

questions.question: The tour guide told us: 'You can take photographs of the traditional costumes, but you must not touch the ancient museum artifacts.' Which reported speech sentence is grammatically correct?

options.text: The tour guide told us that we could take photographs of the traditional costumes, but we must not touch the ancient museum artifacts.
The tour guide told us that we can take photographs of the traditional costumes, but we were not allowed to touch the ancient museum artifacts.
The tour guide told us that we could take photographs of the traditional costumes, but we were not to touch the ancient museum artifacts.
The tour guide told us that we can take photographs of the traditional costumes, but we mustn't touch the ancient museum artifacts.

questions.explanation: In reported speech, modal 'can' backshifts to 'could', while modal prohibition 'must not' remains 'must not' when expressing an ongoing rule or prohibition.

questions.question: Select the option that correctly categorizes the transition words 'furthermore', 'nevertheless', and 'consequently' by their paragraph function in an argumentative essay:
questions.explanation: 'Furthermore' adds supporting ideas, 'nevertheless' introduces a contrasting idea or counterargument, and 'consequently' introduces a logical result or conclusion.

questions.question: Reorder the jumbled words into a syntactically correct Conditional Type 3 sentence: 'national / tourism / Ethiopia / had / revenues / its / expanded / sector / would / heritages / preserved / have / if / .'

options.text: If Ethiopia had preserved its national heritages, tourism revenues would have expanded.
If Ethiopia preserved its national heritages, tourism revenues had expanded.
Tourism revenues had expanded if Ethiopia preserved its national heritages.
Had Ethiopia preserve its national heritages, tourism revenues would expanded.

questions.explanation: Conditional Type 3 syntax requires: 'If' + Subject ('Ethiopia') + Past Perfect ('had preserved') + Object ('its national heritages') + Comma + Main Clause ('tourism revenues would have expanded').
